verdict.reasoning: The patient reports: "I don't really feel like getting up in the morning... I don't have much energy" and later confirms "my mood is lower recently," supporting fatigue and low mood as main concerns.
Duration: The patient says symptoms started around when he began a new job "a couple of months ago" and clarifies "More like two months, I would say. Yeah," matching approximately two months.
He reports difficulty getting up: "I don't really feel like getting up in the morning" and clarifies sleep issues: "I'm just having trouble sleeping at all. Probably."
He states: "I don't have much energy at all during the day" and repeats that he "just don't feel like I have a lot of energy."
He reports decreased appetite: "I'm not eating very much at the moment."

He describes: "Finding it really hard to... quite difficult to keep focusing. I would say not unhappy or happy, but just quite. Just not focused," which the clinician summarizes as "difficulty focusing, quite distracted."
He explicitly says: "actually now you mentioned it, like my mood is lower recently."
He reports reduced sex drive: "Like my sex drive has kind of decreased over the past few months as well" and later, "just over the last few months, just been disinterested."

He states: "when I've been doing sports as well, I find sometimes it's quite difficult to breathe. So I have some kind of like shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago."
Past history: "in the past I have a history of hypothyroidism... Hypo Hypothyroidism..." confirmed by the clinician as "Hypothyroid."
The transcript notes a history of hypothyroidism in past medical history but never shows an explicit assessment section listing it; linking it specifically to an 'assessment' is not stated.
Medication: "I have a drug history of thyroxine" and to "Do you continue to take thyroxine now?" he answers "Yes... So you're taking thyroxine at the moment? Yes."
Family history: "my father has committed suicide about 15 years ago."
The suicide is documented in family history, but the transcript does not show an explicit assessment statement referencing it; saying it is noted in the assessment is extra detail.
Social history: In response to relationship status, he says: "Yeah, I'm married. I've been for many years."
No substance use (alcohol, tobacco, drugs) is mentioned anywhere; asserting "no substance use history" introduces information not discussed.

The patient links timing to a new job: symptoms "might have even coincided with that job a couple of months ago," but the clinician’s assessment never explicitly states fatigue and low mood are correlated with a new job and lifestyle changes.
Decreased libido and low mood are both elicited, but the clinician does not explicitly assess or state that decreased libido is associated with mood changes.

He reports exertional dyspnea progression: "when I've been doing sports... shortness of breath when doing sports compared to maybe a couple of months ago," and the clinician restates: "you've become more short of breath over the last few months."
Hypothyroidism is documented under past medical history, but the assessment portion does not explicitly list or discuss it as part of the assessment.
The family history of suicide is elicited, but the assessment section at the end does not explicitly include or discuss it as part of the assessment.

Plan: "I would like to probably see you in person and do an examination... do you think it'd be possible to... book an appointment in the next few days with your GP... and then we could... do an examination."

The clinician states: "we probably like to do some blood tests as well" and later "do an examination and do some investigations, really, to see what's going on," confirming blood tests to investigate symptoms.
There is no explicit plan stated to monitor mood and energy levels; the clinician mentions further investigations and confirming the patient is not suicidal but not ongoing monitoring instructions.

The consultation is remote and no physical exam is performed or described; the clinician says they would like to "see you in person and do an examination" in the future, indicating no current objective physical findings were discussed.
